story.head: Stephenson’s favorite opponent
paras: The Kraken have won two of the three meetings this season. The Flames (7-8-0) beat San Jose 2-1 on Monday, while the Kraken (8-5-1). This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames sixth (25th in the NHL) and the Kraken third (tied for 15th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Flames’ record (.467) is about what their chances are worth. The Kraken’s record (.607) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.442), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Flames take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (30th). Calgary has scored 2.53 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Kraken keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st), but rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd). They also give up a lot of shots (32nd), so the Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. Seattle has allowed 3.71 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. Both teams like to play fast, especially the Flames (2nd), so expect an open game.

Joel Farabee (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 15 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 15 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Kraken, Chandler Stephenson (2 G / 10 A / 12 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in seven straight games against Calgary. Frédérick Gaudreau (7 G / 3 A / 10 P in 14 GP) has a team-high seven goals.

Dustin Wolf (3-4-0 / .862 SV% in 7 GS) has struggled for Calgary so far, but is expected to start. Joey Daccord (3-3-0 / .880 SV% in 6 GS) is expected to go for Seattle. Wolf has a .862 save percentage in seven starts against the Kraken, well under his usual .902. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Lane Lambert likes to send Winterton, Meyers and Douglas out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Tsyplakov, Castagna and Klapka.
